title: Depth had different links to flash and scene peak times in selected Allen mouse V1 units
abstract: We tested whether depth predicts the same unit's scene-minus-flash peak response time in Allen Visual Coding Neuropixels data. The primary sample had 5991 visual cortical units in 145 probe-area groups from 32 mice. A model with group intercepts gave a slope of 1.77 ms per 100 um, with a 95% whole-mouse bootstrap interval of 0.03 to 3.54. Equal group weighting gave an interval that included zero. In the exploratory six-area analysis, V1 had a slope of 5.98 in 1423 units from 29 mice. Its six-area Bonferroni interval was 2.70 to 9.18. The V1 flash slope was -5.92, while the scene slope was 0.05. Post hoc V1 checks kept positive contrast intervals. The results show different depth associations for the two stimuli in selected V1 units. Peak times are preferred-condition histogram maxima, not response onset. Probe geometry, cell composition, response noise and behavior limit inference. No direct synaptic graph or independent recording was tested. Original code, aggregate results, bootstrap estimates, source hashes, a figure and external retrieval instructions support reproduction.

display.caption: Scene-minus-flash peak-time depth slopes. Bars show pointwise 95% whole-mouse bootstrap intervals. The pooled contrast is sensitive to weights. V1 is an exploratory area result; its six-area interval is reported in the text.
